venue: Natural Language Processing and Chinese Computing
reason: Propõe a defesa SafeCoT, além de uma taxonomia de ataques e um dataset de prompts jailbreak. A abordagem é avaliada em dez ataques e três LLMs, com resultados sobre redução de ASR e manutenção de desempenho geral.

title: Boosting Jailbreak Transferability for Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models have heightened concerns regarding safety alignment challenges, particularly stemming from jailbreak attacks that circumvent security measures to generate malicious outputs. To address the limitations of existing methods such as GCG, which achieve strong performance on specific models but suffer from efficacy degradation and poor transferability on unseen models, we propose a novel jailbreak method extending GCG. This approach integrates three core components: a scenario induction template, optimized suffix selection, and the re-suffix attack mechanism to minimize output inconsistencies. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method, achieving near-perfect success rates (approaching 100%) in both direct attacks and cross-model transferability.
authors: Jian ZhengHanqing LiuLifeng ZhouHuanqian YanPeilin Liu
venue: Pattern Recognition and Computer Vision
reason: O estudo propõe um novo método de jailbreak voltado a aumentar eficácia e transferibilidade entre modelos. O resumo relata experimentos extensos em diferentes benchmarks e altas taxas de sucesso, oferecendo evidência direta sobre mecanismos e avaliação de ataques.

title: JailbreakMaster: Low-Interaction Jailbreak Prompt Generation via Feature-Guided Strategy Search and Adaptive Fusion
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit strong generative capabilities yet remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks that undermine safety and reliability. Existing jailbreak methods often require excessive interactions or computational resources, limiting practicality for real-world use. We present Jailbreak-Master, an automated framework for low-interaction jailbreak prompt generation via feature-guided strategy search over an extensible strategy hub, with adaptive fusion as a complementary enhancement. JailbreakMaster models target-side textual features to index and select strategies and composes them to generate adversarial prompts under black-box settings. Experiments indicate that, across closed-source models such as GPT-4, Gemini Pro, and DeepSeek V3, JailbreakMaster achieves an average attack success rate above 73% while typically completing successful attacks in fewer than ten target-model queries. On open-source models, it attains an even higher average success rate of about 93% and also demonstrates robustness against common defenses. Together, these results establish JailbreakMaster as an efficient and practical framework for automated, low-interaction jailbreak prompt generation.
authors: Ba, Zezhi and Zhao, Jiawei and Chen, Kejiang and Zhang, Weiming and Yu, Nenghai
venue: 2025 International Conference on Cyber Resilience and Endogenous Safety & Security (CRESS)
reason: O jailbreak é o foco central, com um framework automatizado para geração de prompts adversariais em cenário black-box. O estudo fornece resultados de ASR, número de consultas, avaliação em modelos abertos e fechados e análise frente a defesas comuns.

title: A Study on Cross-Lingual Security Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
abstract: In this study, we look at how Large Language Models (LLMs) trained mostly in English react to prompt injection (PI) attacks written in other languages, especially Turkish. We tested several open-weight models such as Gemma3n-e4b, Gemma3-27b, and Llama3.3-70b. In our tests, we compared direct and indirect attacks and tried simple defenses. The results show that direct attacks are usually stronger, reaching more than 90% success in bigger models. Indirect attacks are weaker but still a real risk. We also saw that English prompts often succeed more than Turkish ones, but this gap becomes smaller as the model size grows. Current defenses only lower the risk a little and sometimes even make it worse. Our study shows that LLM security depends on both language and model size, and that better multilingual defenses are needed.
authors: Özçelik, Melik Buğra and Şentaş, Ali and Koçyiğit, Berkecan and Özen, Sinan and Akmeşe, Arda
venue: 2025 16th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
reason: O estudo testa explicitamente ataques de prompt injection diretos e indiretos em vários LLMs, compara idiomas e avalia defesas simples. Relata taxas de sucesso e diferenças entre modelos e idiomas, oferecendo evidência experimental diretamente alinhada à revisão.

title: FuzzLLM: A Novel and Universal Fuzzing Framework for Proactively Discovering Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
abstract: Jailbreak vulnerabilities in Large Language Models (LLMs), which exploit meticulously crafted prompts to elicit content that violates service guidelines, have captured the attention of research communities. While model owners can defend against individual jailbreak prompts through safety training strategies, this relatively passive approach struggles to handle the broader category of similar jailbreaks. To tackle this issue, we introduce FuzzLLM, an automated fuzzing framework designed to proactively test and discover jailbreak vulnerabilities in LLMs. We utilize templates to capture the structural integrity of a prompt and isolate key features of a jailbreak class as constraints. By integrating different base classes into powerful combo attacks and varying the elements of constraints and prohibited questions, FuzzLLM enables efficient testing with reduced manual effort. Extensive experiments demonstrate FuzzLLM’s effectiveness and comprehensiveness in vulnerability discovery across various LLMs.
authors: Yao, Dongyu and Zhang, Jianshu and Harris, Ian G. and Carlsson, Marcel
venue: ICASSP 2024 - 2024 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
reason: Propõe um framework automatizado de fuzzing para descobrir vulnerabilidades de jailbreak, incluindo templates, classes de ataques e combinações automatizadas. Relata experimentos extensivos em vários LLMs, oferecendo evidência relevante sobre geração e avaliação sistemática de ataques.

title: Safety Alignment Should be Made More than just A Few Attention Heads
abstract: Safety alignment in large language models (LLMs) remains vulnerable, as adversarial prompts can bypass their safety measures. We find that safety mechanisms are concentrated in a small subset of attention heads, and ablating these heads severely compromises model safety. To identify these critical components, we introduce RDSHA, a targeted ablation method that leverages the model’s refusal direction. Our analysis reveals that existing jailbreak attacks exploit this concentration by manipulating these specific heads. To mitigate this, we propose AHD, a training strategy to distribute safety behaviors across numerous attention heads. Experiments show that models trained with AHD achieve significantly stronger robustness against mainstream jailbreak attacks, successfully distributing safety capabilities across attention heads, while maintaining overall model utility.
authors: Huang, Chao and Zhang, Zefeng and Yue, Juwei and Sheng, Jiawei and Li, Quangang and Zhang, Chuang and Liu, Tingwen
venue: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
reason: O estudo investiga diretamente como jailbreaks exploram a concentração de mecanismos de segurança em poucos attention heads e propõe uma estratégia de treinamento para aumentar a robustez. Apresenta mecanismo de exploração, defesa e avaliação experimental contra ataques de jailbreak.

title: Exploring the Essence of Prompt Tone: A Comparative Study of Large Language Model Security
abstract: Chatbots powered by Large Language Model(LLM) can be manipulated by malicious prompts, generating harmful content and biased responses which would raise security concerns. Growing dependence on chatbots demands robust security for ethical development and user trust, which makes the work relevant in today’s world. The motivation behind the work is to let the user have a safe experience with no negative responses being displayed while using the chatbot, which paved the way to arrive at the goal of developing a security filter that could be integrated into any LLM feature integrated application to mitigate the risk of having security vulnerabilities like prompt injection and jailbreaking, which could be achieved by converting malicious prompt into safer prompts by the method of eliminating negative sentiment phrases. The work focuses on building and implementing the security filters to popular in-production LLMs like Large Language Model Meta AI-2 (LLaMA2) and Generative Pre-trained Transformer – 3.5 turbo (GPT-3.5) to see how they handle against prompt injection and jailbreaking before and after the security filter being integrated. A large database of 200,000 prompts has been collected and preprocessed to train on a machine learning model using binary classification algorithm having 99.7% accuracy for classification of prompts into malicious or non-malicious and further checks are being done by breaking the prompt into smaller phrases and individually analyzing their compound sentiment score using Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK) Valence Aware Dictionary for Sentiment Reasoning (VADER) algorithm to detect and drop the negative sentiment phrases for the modification of the user prompt to eliminate the possibility of malicious prompt being passed to LLM. It is difficult to determine the sentiment of prompts in a detailed way and convert it into an efficient design that will perform well with models. Once this hurdle is overcome, chatbots will become even more reliable, trustworthy, and user-friendly tools, increasing the level of people’s trust in this technology, and establishing guidelines for how to use these resources in the most beneficial ways.
authors: Nair, Aiswarya and Vithayathil, Jose and Nambiar, Sandeep Prem and S, Snehasree and Murali, Shalu
venue: 2024 Third International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Information and Communication Technologies (ICEEICT)
reason: Desenvolve um filtro de segurança para prompt injection e jailbreak, combinando classificação de prompts e remoção de frases com sentimento negativo. O trabalho relata uma base de 200.000 prompts, experimentos com LLaMA2 e GPT-3.5 e métricas quantitativas.

title: Jailbreaking Large Language Models: Safety Alignment, Response Quality, Computational Cost
abstract: Large language models are often equipped with safety alignment mechanisms designed to prevent generation of harmful or other unwanted content. However, an increasing number of jailbreaking techniques attempt to circumvent these safeguards, raising significant safety concerns. This paper introduces an open-source evaluation framework that analyzes jailbreaking effectiveness in several dimensions: refusal bypass rate, harmful response quality, impact on general model capabilities, and computational cost. In the study, prompt injection, sampling exploits, and model manipulation techniques are examined across four open-weight instruction-tuned large language models. The results demonstrate that high refusal bypass does not necessarily equate to practical safety compromise. Specifically, model manipulation methods like single refusal direction ablation achieve a high attack success rate, but often degrade general capabilities and require significant computational resources. Meanwhile, sampling-based exploits show a minimal practical threat when assessed with a robust model classifier. The findings emphasize the importance of comprehensive, multi-dimensional evaluation to accurately characterize jailbreaking effectiveness and safety risks in large language models.
authors: Rosengren, Jonas and Brynielsson, Joel and Johansson, Fredrik and Jonell, Patrik
venue: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications (ICMLA)
reason: O estudo avalia diretamente técnicas de jailbreak, incluindo prompt injection, em quatro LLMs e propõe uma avaliação multidimensional de efetividade, qualidade, impacto e custo. A forte evidência experimental e a comparação de mecanismos de ataque tornam o trabalho diretamente útil para questões sobre ataques, métricas e protocolos de avaliação.

title: Adaptive and Privacy-Preserving Detection of Evolving Prompt Injection Attacks in Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive abilities but are extremely vulnerable to prompt injection attacks where malicious inputs bypass the intended instructions, bypass safety mechanisms, or leak sensitive data. Current defences have two severe shortcomings: they are fixed and unresponsive to new attack techniques like obfuscation and multi-turn manipulation, and frequently they impact the privacy of the user by sending unprocessed queries to third-party validation services. Such constraints render existing solutions inappropriate to real-world, privacy-aware activities. This research suggests a privacy-sensitive and adaptive detection architecture that combines continual learning and context-sensitive embeddings, and federated detection pipelines. The framework becomes flexible to new adversarial actions and provides local data confidentiality. According to experimental findings, the detection accuracy is 94.8% and the false positive rate is 4.1, which is higher than that of baseline methods, meanwhile, the obfuscation attack and multi-turn attacks are detected more, with gains of 12.4 and 15.7 percentage points respectively, and latency is real-time (112 ms/query). The model provides a measurable and reliable framework of securing systems powered by LLM.
authors: Depuru, SivaKumar and Lakshmi, Kurugunda Radha and Chandrahas, Gopa and Chetana, Mopuri and Reddy, Madduri Vinay Krishna
venue: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Communication Networks and Application (ICSCN)
reason: O estudo propõe uma arquitetura adaptativa e preservadora de privacidade para detectar prompt injection, incluindo ofuscação e manipulação multi-turn. Relata acurácia, falsos positivos, ganhos por tipo de ataque e latência, oferecendo evidência experimental diretamente relevante.

title: Defending Large Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks Through Chain of Thought Prompting
abstract: With the deep research and widespread application of Large Language Models (LLMs), the security and privacy issues inherent in them have gradually become prominent, posing new challenges in the field of network security. Elaborately designed jailbreak attack prompts may induce LLMs to act against human values and preferences and generate harmful responses. To address this issue, we introduce a straightforward yet effective defence mechanism: Chain of Thought Prompting. This defence mechanism aims to emulate human thought processess. Chain of Thought Prompting method fully harnesses the inherent reasoning ability of the LLMs via five stages. It encourages Large Language Models (LLMs) to engage in self-thought, self-reflection, and self-refinement. Our experiments on ChatGLM-3-6B and Llama-2-7B-Chat, utilizing the JADE and DAN datasets, demonstrate a significant reduction in the average Attack Success Rate (ASR) for jailbreak attacks. This reduction is from 65.01% to 13.40% for ChatGLM-3-6B, and from 49.06% to 0.13% for Llama-2-7B-Chat. Our findings suggest that Chain of Thought Prompting can significantly reduce the generation of harmful content. Our work provides an effective method for LLMs to counter jailbreak attacks, enhancing the safety of LLMs without the need for additional training.
authors: Cao, Yanfei and Gu, Naijie and Shen, Xinyue and Yang, Daiyuan and Zhang, Xingmin
venue: 2024 International Conference on Networking and Network Applications (NaNA)
reason: Propõe diretamente uma defesa contra jailbreak baseada em Chain of Thought Prompting e a avalia em dois LLMs e dois datasets. O resumo fornece Attack Success Rate antes e depois da defesa, tornando a contribuição especialmente relevante para avaliação de mitigação.

title: Watch Your Words: Successfully Jailbreak LLM by Mitigating the “Prompt Malice”
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown outstanding generative and contextual understanding capabilities, and have been widely used and deployed in various applications. Alignment can significantly enhance the security of LLM. However, even aligned LLMs are still vulnerable to persistent jailbreak attacks. In this paper, we propose a novel jailbreak attack against LLMs. We observe that kind words have an inducing effect, which can be leveraged to increase the attack success rate of jailbreaks. Based on the above observations, we combine multiple strategies to propose a jailbreak attack based on textual malice mitigation. Experiments on various LLMs demonstrate that a high success rate of the attack can be achieved across different models. Additionally, we conduct zero-shot and few-shot experiments on the jailbreak results, which show that although aligned LLMs can distinguish malicious outputs, they may still be misled by carefully constructed prompts. This conclusion also provides a new perspective for understanding the security mechanisms of LLMs.
authors: Xiaowei XuYixiao XuXiong ChenPeng ChenMohan LiYanbin Sun
venue: Web and Big Data
reason: O artigo propõe diretamente um ataque de jailbreak baseado em mitigação da malícia textual e combina múltiplas estratégias de construção de prompts. O resumo relata experimentos em vários LLMs, altas taxas de sucesso e avaliações zero-shot e few-shot.

title: Defending Against GCG Jailbreak Attacks with Syntax Trees and Perplexity in LLMs
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel classification method that utilizes syntax trees and perplexity to identify jailbreak attacks that use hostile suffixes to make large language models (LLMs) more likely to generate dangerous content, such as Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) attacks. GCG jailbreak attacks deceive the model with hostile suffixes, prompting LLMs to produce responses that exceed ethical limits. To address this issue, we propose a classifier that can confirm whether the input to the LLM contains a suffix indicative of a GCG jailbreak attack. The STPC (Syntax Trees and Perplexity Classifier) introduces syntax trees to analyze the structural characteristics of GCG suffixes and combines perplexity for comprehensive classification judgment. It accurately detects most jailbreak attacks in the test set, mitigates false positives, and improves the reliability of LLM responses. In all STPC test results, the classification accuracy reached 96.2%.
authors: Chen, Qiuyu and Yamaguchi, Shingo and Yamamoto, Yudai
venue: 2024 IEEE 13th Global Conference on Consumer Electronics (GCCE)
reason: Investiga diretamente a detecção de ataques jailbreak GCG por meio de árvores sintáticas e perplexidade. O resumo descreve mecanismo de ataque, método defensivo e avaliação quantitativa com acurácia de classificação.

title: Transferable Ensemble Black-Box Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
abstract: We propose a novel black-box jailbreak attacking framework that incorporates various LLM-as-Attacker methods to deliver transferable and powerful jailbreak attacks. Our method is driven by three key observations from existing jailbreaking studies and practices. First, an ensemble of multiple attack methods is more effective in exposing vulnerabilities of aligned LLMs than single attack methods, as it can cover diverse weaknesses in the target model's defense mechanism. Second, different malicious instructions inherently vary in their jailbreaking difficulty, necessitating differentiated treatment to ensure more efficient attacks. Finally, the semantic coherence of a malicious instruction is crucial for triggering the defenses of an aligned LLM; therefore, it must be carefully disrupted to manipulate its embedding representation, thereby increasing the jailbreak success rate. Experimental results validate the framework's superiority: it achieves strong jailbreak performance across diverse target LLMs, with notable improvements in transferability compared to baseline methods, and maintains high stealthiness as measured by semantic similarity metrics. Notably, with this framework, we won the championship in the jailbreaking attack track of a global LLM safety competition and received the best black-box method honor, validating its practical superiority.
authors: Chen, Xiaoxiao and Qian, Jingwei and Wang, Haitao
venue: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Security and Governance (ICAISG)
reason: Propõe um framework black-box de jailbreak que combina múltiplos métodos de ataque e busca aumentar transferibilidade e furtividade. O resumo relata avaliação experimental contra diversos LLMs e métricas de desempenho e similaridade semântica.

title: KG-Guard: Dynamic Knowledge Graph-Guided Multi-Turn Jailbreak Defense Framework for Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly vulnerable to multi-turn jailbreak attacks that exploit accumulated conversational context to bypass safety constraints. These progressive attacks challenge existing defenses, which often rely on static filters or per-turn steering and lack awareness of long-range semantic evolution. We propose KG-Guard, a dynamic knowledge graph-guided defense framework that models entity-relation evolution across dialogue turns. By incrementally constructing a conversation-level knowledge graph (KG), KGGuard identifies emerging relational patterns that converge toward unsafe objectives. A novel Relation-Convergence Detector (RCD) integrates rule-based path matching and neural graph reasoning to assess convergence risk, enabling proactive intervention through prompt re-steering or response regulation. Experiments on benchmark multi-turn jailbreak datasets show that KG-Guard achieves superior robustness and interpretability, reducing Attack Success Rate (ASR) by 5-8% compared with state-of-the-art defenses while maintaining dialogue fluency.
authors: Zou, Xide
venue: 2025 6th International Conference on Machine Learning and Computer Application (ICMLCA)
reason: O artigo propõe uma defesa específica para jailbreak multi-turn baseada em grafos de conhecimento e detector de convergência relacional. Apresenta experimentos em benchmarks, comparação com defesas de estado da arte e redução de ASR, fornecendo evidência diretamente útil.

title: Assessing and Mitigating Multi-Turn Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models: A Crescendo Attack Study
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are vulnerable to multi-turn jailbreak attacks like Crescendo, which exploit context retention to bypass safety mechanisms and generate harmful outputs. This study is among the first to address the gap in understanding vulnerabilities of LLMs released after 2024 by reproducing the Crescendo attack on six recent models. We introduce two novel mitigation strategies—prompt hardening and LLM-as-guardrail—evaluated via Attack Success Rates (ASRs) across 15 tasks. Our contributions include these mitigation strategies, a comprehensive vulnerability assessment, and an open-source framework shared under the MIT License to foster collaborative AI safety research. Findings reveal that Llama-3.1-8b-Instruct (Llama 3.1) was the most resistant, achieving the lowest ASRs in 9 of 15 categories due to robust safety alignment, while DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B (DeepSeek R1) was highly vulnerable with 1.0 ASRs in 13 categories. Prompt hardening significantly outperformed LLM-as-guardrail, reducing ASRs effectively across models, though DeepSeek R1 maintained 1.0 ASRs despite mitigations. These results underscore prompt hardening as a superior defense, enhancing LLM security for safer deployment in critical domains like healthcare, education, and public policy.
authors: Saad, Muhammad and Mughal, Shafaq Fatima and Mustafa, Muhammad and Ahmed, Ikhlas and Masood, Adnan
venue: 2025 27th International Multitopic Conference (INMIC)
reason: O estudo avalia diretamente um jailbreak multi-turn (Crescendo) em seis LLMs e testa duas estratégias de mitigação com ASR em 15 tarefas. O ataque, as defesas e a avaliação experimental são centrais, embora o contexto seja geral de LLMs conversacionais.

title: Enhancing System Security: LLM-Driven Defense Against Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities
abstract: This article examines cybersecurity vulnerabilities in systems utilizing Language Model Interfaces, focusing on the challenges of building secure systems. It provides an overview of current interfaces and their associated risks. A key contribution is the design of a prompt analysis and injection detection subsystem, which assesses input relevance and security. The integration of an additional Filter level in the system safeguards against prompt injection attacks by pre-processing user requests and post-processing responses. This level includes a Prompt Analyzer for input wrapping, and an Attack Validator module using the LLM to classify prompts. The study evaluates various prompt injection attacks across different system setups, including core GPT -3 and GPT-4 models without additional security layers, a Fuzzy Search method, and systems using an Attack Validator based on GPT-3 and GPT -4 models.
authors: Muliarevych, Oleksandr
venue: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Advanced Trends in Radioelectronics, Telecommunications and Computer Engineering (TCSET)
reason: Prompt injection é o foco central e o trabalho propõe uma camada de filtragem com análise e validação de ataques. O resumo também relata avaliação de diferentes ataques e configurações envolvendo GPT-3 e GPT-4.

title: Learning from Literature: A Retraining-Free Framework for LLM Jailbreak Defense via NLP-Based Adversarial Literature Analysis
abstract: Recent surge in adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) have made them vulnerable to sophisticated adversarial attacks, manipulative prompts, and encoded malicious inputs. Existing countermeasures often require retraining models, a process that is computationally expensive and impractical for deployment. This paper introduces a novel defense framework that enables LLMs to autonomously detect, filter, and fend off malicious or adversarial inputs without requiring retraining or fine-tuning. The proposed framework consists of two core components: (1) A summarization module that processes and summarizes adversarial research literature to provide the LLM with context-aware defense knowledge and (2) A prompt filtering module that detects, decodes, and classifies harmful inputs through advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques, such as zero-shot classification, keyword analysis, and encoded content detection. By combining text extraction, summarization, and malicious prompt analysis, this approach enhances the robustness of LLMs against adversarial misuse. Experimental results demonstrate that this integrated approach successfully identifies encoded prompts, malicious patterns, and manipulative language structures with a success rate of 98.7%. The framework also enables the model to respond appropriately to malicious prompts with a higher percentage of jailbreak resistance and refusal rate, using minimal quantity of adversarial research literature as context. The framework significantly reduces LLM Attack Success Rate (ASR) as a lightweight, efficient alternative to retraining-based time and resource-consuming defenses, while upholding LLM response quality.
authors: Muhaimin, Sheikh Samit and Mastorakis, Spyridon
venue: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Trust, Privacy and Security in Intelligent Systems, and Applications (TPS-ISA)
reason: O estudo propõe uma defesa retraining-free contra jailbreak e entradas adversariais, combinando análise de literatura com detecção, decodificação e filtragem de prompts maliciosos. Apresenta resultados quantitativos de detecção, resistência a jailbreak e redução de ASR, sendo diretamente relevante para estratégias de defesa e avaliação.

title: Security Posture Evaluation of Model Context Protocol Servers Against Prompt Injection
abstract: This study presents a security-oriented evaluation of the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard enabling large language models (LLMs) to interface with external tools through structured interactions. The experiment was deployed in a controlled environment using an open-source MCP server with basic file manipulation tools. A set of prompt injection tests was designed to probe the system's ability to handle adversarial instructions, ambiguous input, and encoded payloads. Despite expectations, the system failed to reject adversarial instructions embedded in user input and did not detect anomalous tool usage patterns-such as suspicious parameters. These failures underscore the current vulnerability of LLM-tool integrations to prompt injection threats. The results highlight the urgent need for defense-in-depth strategies within MCP implementations, including stricter input validation, contextaware filtering, strong access control policies and transparent logging. Collectively, these measures are essential for securing AI-assisted tool chains against emerging adversarial techniques.
authors: Tod-Raileanu, Gabriela and Axinte, Sabina-Daniela and Dincă, Ana-Maria and Bacivarov, Ioan C.
venue: 2025 IEEE 31st International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
reason: O artigo avalia diretamente prompt injection em um servidor MCP com ferramentas externas, incluindo instruções adversariais, entradas ambíguas e payloads codificados. O experimento evidencia falhas de rejeição e uso anômalo de ferramentas e discute medidas de defesa.

title: Prompt Injection as the New SQL Injection: The Emergence of Attacks on AI Reasoning
abstract: The introduction of Large Language Models (LLMs) into enterprise application pipelines represents both a blessing and a curse — the same versatility in following instructions that enables conversational assistants, code copilots, and autonomous agents also erodes the distinction between trusted instruction and untrusted data. In this paper, we argue that Prompt Injection (PI) follows SQL Injection (SQLi) as a fundamental class of attack on machine learning systems. While SQLi leveraged the absence of distinction between code and data in relation queries, PI leverages the absence of separation between system instruction and contextual data in natural language reasoning. The target domain has shifted from syntactic parsing to semantic interpretation, and classic defenses — escaping, parameterization, and whitelisting — are insufficient because natural language lacks a formal grammar to sanitize. We perform a narrative analysis of relevant peer-reviewed and preprint publications within the period 2023–2026, structured around three major dimensions: (i) the taxonomy of direct and indirect prompt injection attacks, (ii) the tactics that PI employs to overcome defenses provided by Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and guardrails, and (iii) the elevated threat landscape of agentic LLM applications with tool capabilities. We formalize the attacker’s strategic edge through a success rate model and offer comparative studies with SQLi, a severity scale for different modes of operation, and guidance for Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs). Our core thesis is that PI represents a paradigm shift, necessitating defense strategies beyond input sanitization toward workflow isolation and defensive LLMs.
authors: Abzal, Shuktaev and Bakhtiyar, Karabalin and Sultan, Orynbasar and Orlova, Olga and Korochkina, Elena Aleksandrovna and Borashova, Sholpan
venue: 2026 International Conference on Cybersecurity, Digital Forensics, and AI Applications (ICCSDFAI)
reason: Prompt injection é o tema central, analisado por meio de uma síntese narrativa estruturada sobre ataques diretos e indiretos, evasão de guardrails e riscos em aplicações agentic. O trabalho também apresenta taxonomia, comparação com SQL injection e orientações defensivas, sendo potencialmente útil para várias perguntas da revisão.

title: Red-Team Prompt Injection Defense Using Multi-Context Protocol (MCP)
abstract: Prompt injection attacks represent a critical security risk in Large Language Model (LLM)–powered applications, enabling adversaries to manipulate model behavior, bypass safety controls, and trigger unauthorized actions. Existing defenses predominantly rely on prompt hardening or output filtering, which remain brittle against adaptive and indirect attack techniques. This paper introduces a red-team–driven defense framework based on a Multi-Context Protocol (MCP) that enforces strict isolation and validation of prompt layers. MCP separates system, developer, retrieval, and user prompts into independently trusted contexts and applies context validation, version control, semantic consistency checks, and input reputation scoring prior to model inference. Through empirical evaluation using representative prompt injection attacks, the proposed approach demonstrates a significant reduction in successful injection attempts while preserving low latency and minimal false positives. The framework is model-agnostic and designed for secure deployment in enterprise and regulated LLM environments.
authors: Jadav, VasanthRao and Bussari, Shravya and Aurangabadkar, Mukesh and Garg, Anshul
venue: SoutheastCon 2026
reason: Prompt injection é o foco central e o trabalho propõe isolamento e validação de diferentes camadas de contexto, incluindo prompts de retrieval. O resumo informa avaliação empírica com ataques representativos, embora forneça menos detalhes experimentais que outros estudos primários.

title: Adversarial and Multilingual Threats in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: From Prompt Injection to Model Exploitation
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have emerged as a cornerstone of modern generative AI by coupling large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge retrieval, thereby enabling more grounded, accurate, and context-aware outputs. Yet this paradigm simultaneously broadens the attack surface—extending vulnerabilities from generation into retrieval pipelines, language interfaces, and exposed APIs. In this paper, we propose a comprehensive threat taxonomy and adversarial framework targeting both conventional and agentic RAG systems, in which LLMs autonomously plan and execute multi-step tasks using retrieved knowledge. Our analysis spans a wide spectrum of adversarial techniques, including prompt injection, jailbreak exploits, API-driven model extraction, and multilingual prompt manipulation. Unlike prior work that primarily focuses on English-only vulnerabilities, we show that multilingual RAG pipelines—particularly those involving language blending (e.g., Arabic-English code-switching)—introduce novel attack vectors that bypass safety filters and induce unintended behaviors. To study these risks, we develop a multilingual adversarial benchmark suite that integrates both synthetic and real-world corpora across English, Arabic, and Spanish. Through systematic evaluation, we demonstrate how the retrieval layer not only amplifies leakage and inversion risks but also enables adversaries to infer system logic, extract private data from vector stores, and manipulate autonomous agent behavior through tool-integrated APIs. To mitigate these threats, we assess multiple defense strategies, including prompt sanitization, cross-lingual content filtering, retriever-stage anomaly detection, and behavior-based profiling of API interactions. Our findings reveal that existing safeguards are insufficient—particularly in agentic or low-resource language scenarios—underscoring the need for architecture-specific and multilingual defenses. This work fills a critical gap in GenAI security by presenting the first holistic, multilingual, and agent-aware security framework for RAG, offering actionable guidance for building robust and trustworthy generative AI applications across diverse linguistic and deployment contexts.
authors: ElSaify, Basma and Baderelden, Mohamed
venue: 2025 2nd International Generative AI and Computational Language Modelling Conference (GACLM)
reason: O estudo investiga ameaças em RAG convencional e agentic, incluindo prompt injection, jailbreak, extração de modelo e manipulação multilíngue. Propõe taxonomia e framework adversarial, cria benchmark multilíngue e avalia várias estratégias de defesa, alinhando-se fortemente ao foco em conteúdo externo e RAG.

title: MedRAGShield: A Three-Tier Defense Framework Against Document Poisoning and Adversarial Attacks in Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems deployed in medical question-answering applications introduce novel attack surfaces not addressed by existing large language model (LLM) safety mechanisms. This research presents MedRAGShield, a three-tier middleware defense framework designed to detect and neutralise document injection poisoning, hallucination exploitation, prompt injection, and jailbreak attacks against medical RAG pipelines. The proposed system operates across three independently togglable defense modes: a baseline mode with no filtering, a confidence and hallucination gating mode, and a full defense mode augmenting the prior modes with Domain-Aware Sanity Check (DASC) rules that apply medical ontological constraints to generated outputs. This experiment constructs a 40-query adversarial evaluation dataset spanning four attack categories and conducts an empirical evaluation on a clinical pharmacology RAG system built on Llama 3.2:3B and ChromaDB. Results demonstrate that confidence-based defenses alone are insufficient against high-similarity document poisoning attacks, which achieve retrieval confidence exceeding 0.85 while delivering clinically dangerous misinformation, a phenomenon this research terms the high-confidence poisoning paradox. The full MedRAGShield defense reduces Attack Success Rate (ASR) from 13.2% (undefended) to 0.0%, with block rate increasing from 0% to 62.5%, while maintaining sub-second query latency. This work establishes a reproducible evaluation methodology for medical RAG security and identifies domain-specific semantic rule checking as a critical missing layer in current LLM defense architectures. Code, dataset, and defense rules are openly available.
authors: Shanid, Mohammed and Prasad, Gaurav and Bawgi, Veeresh and Gowda, Srujan
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Emerging Synergy Science and Technology (ICESST)
reason: Propõe uma defesa para RAG médico contra document poisoning, prompt injection, jailbreak e outros ataques. Traz dataset adversarial, metodologia reproduzível e resultados de ASR, sendo especialmente relevante pelo contexto de documentos recuperados e conteúdo externo.

title: AttnTrace: Contextual Attribution of Prompt Injection and Knowledge Corruption
abstract: Long-context large language models (LLMs), such as GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Pro, and Claude-Sonnet-4, are increasingly used to empower advanced AI systems, including retrievalaugmented generation (RAG) systems and autonomous agents. In these systems, an LLM receives an instruction along with a context-often consisting of texts retrieved from a knowledge database, memory, or the Internet-and generates a response that is contextually grounded by following the instruction. Many recent studies showed that these LLM-empowered systems are vulnerable to prompt injection and knowledge corruption attacks, where an attacker can inject malicious texts into the context such that the LLM generates an output as the attacker desires. One important research question is how to trace back to these malicious texts from a long context in leading to the attacker-desired output of the LLM. While significant efforts have been made, state-of-the-art solutions still achieve a sub-optimal performance and/or incur high computation cost. In this work, we propose AttnTrace, a new context traceback method based on the attention weights produced by an LLM for a prompt. To effectively utilize attention weights, we introduce two techniques designed to enhance the effectiveness of AttnTrace, and we provide theoretical insights for our design choice. We also perform a systematic evaluation for AttnTrace. The results demonstrate that AttnTrace is more accurate and efficient than existing state-of-the-art context traceback methods. We also show AttnTrace can improve state-of-the-art methods in detecting prompt injection under long contexts through the attribution-before-detection paradigm. As a real-world application, we demonstrate that AttnTrace can effectively pinpoint injected instructions in a paper designed to manipulate LLM-generated reviews. The code and data are available: https://github.com/Wang-Yanting/AttnTrace.
authors: Wang, Yanting and Geng, Runpeng and Chen, Ying and Jia, Jinyuan
venue: 2026 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
reason: Prompt injection is a major focus alongside knowledge corruption, with a method for tracing malicious context and improving injection detection. The study is especially relevant to RAG and agents using retrieved or Internet content and reports systematic comparative evaluation.

title: A Secure and Effective Framework for Key Concept Mining from Educational Content Using Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly prevalent in educational systems, with significant potential to enhance learning experiences through various applications. However, their integration into educational environments can introduce security vulnerabilities, thereby threatening the reliability and integrity of the learning process. Despite the growing adoption of LLMs in education, domain-specific threat assessment for educational applications remains significantly underexplored. To address this gap, we developed a secure educational LLM framework for lecture summarization through systematic threat modeling using the OWASP risk rating methodology. Our analysis identified five major vulnerabilities, among which “prompt injection” was ranked as the highest-severity risk, particularly affecting student interfaces, where malicious inputs could compromise system behavior and educational content integrity. We evaluated an effective defense mechanism known as semantic smoothing, against 20 adversarial prompts across five state-of-the-art LLM models, namely, GPT-4o, GPT-5, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1, Deepseek-llm-7b-chat, Falcon-7b-instruct. The results show that defense effectiveness is highly dependent on the model. GPT-5 achieved optimal protection (HCR reduced from 45% to 30%), while Deepseek-llm-7b-chat showed counterproductive regression under perturbations. These findings demonstrate that robust mitigation strategies must consider the characteristics of individual models, as defenses may vary widely in effectiveness across different LLM architectures.
authors: Abdul Rasheed, Ashika Sameem and Mehedy Masud, Mohammad
venue: 2025 IEEE 19th International Conference on Application of Information and Communication Technologies (AICT)
reason: O estudo trata segurança de uma aplicação de mineração de conceitos e sumarização educacional, identificando prompt injection como risco de maior severidade e avaliando semantic smoothing como defesa. A avaliação cobre 20 prompts adversariais em cinco LLMs e reporta variação de eficácia entre modelos.

title: GRED: Gradual Jailbreak Attack via Relational Decomposition on Large Language Model
abstract: Jailbreak attack is effective in verifying the security of large language models (LLMs). With the development of LLMs, an increasing number of jailbreak attack methods have been proposed to explore the security boundaries of LLMs. Most existing methods employ more universal black-box approaches, that is, using carefully constructed prompts to bypass the security mechanisms of LLMs, enabling the models to answer malicious questions. Previous methods have attempted techniques such as specific templates and semantic obfuscation to transform the original questions into transition questions and achieve jailbreak attacks through multi-round dialogues. However, they lack to guarantee of semantic coherence and purpose consistency throughout the process. Our method uses an attack LLM, starts from the semantic perspective, extracting multiple entity-relation-entity triples from the original question and generating subquestions based on these triples. By sending these sub-questions to the target model, we create a context with background knowledge related to the original question. Then, we summarize the context and gradually generate transition questions with reference to the semantics of the original question, guiding the target LLM to answer the original question, thus completing the jailbreak attack. We call this jailbreak attack GRED (Gradual jailbreak attack based on Relational Decomposition). We conducted extensive experiments on AdvBench, and the results demonstrate that our method achieves the state-of-the-art performance.Warning: This paper contains malicious content from some model outputs.
authors: Zou, Xide and Wang, Dongyu and Tang, Chaoxing and Zhang, Lan
venue: 2026 29th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
reason: Propõe um ataque de jailbreak gradual baseado em decomposição relacional e diálogos multi-turn. O método é avaliado experimentalmente no AdvBench e comparado com abordagens existentes.

title: Detection of Prompt Injection Attacks Using a Hierarchical Approach
abstract: Large Language Models are vulnerable to prompt injection attacks. Although various detection techniques have been proposed, approaches relying on external classifiers are limited by high computational overhead. Accordingly, this paper proposes Multi-layer Hierarchical Detection, a fast and lightweight method that utilizes hidden states from each Transformer layer to perform classification. This method reduces the average number of classification layers required for detection by 75.3 % to 88.5 % compared to the baseline method, while maintaining performance within a marginal F 1 -score difference of 0.5 %. Consequently, the proposed method reduces detection latency and provides an efficient solution.
authors: Lee, Sujin and Pak, Wooguil
venue: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Information and Communication (ICAIIC)
reason: O foco é detectar prompt injection por classificação hierárquica de estados ocultos de camadas Transformer. O resumo apresenta resultados quantitativos de eficiência, latência e F1, indicando avaliação empírica direta.

title: HiddenGuard: Real-Time Detection and Mitigation of Steganographic Prompt Injection Attacks in Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) enable powerful cross-modal reasoning but expose new security risks. One such threat is steganographic prompt injection, where malicious instructions are hidden in images. Existing defenses either incur high latency or fail to detect sophisticated attacks. We propose HiddenGuard, a real-time detection framework integrating (1) cross-modal consistency analysis, (2) wavelet-based steganographic detection, and (3) context-aware threat assessment. HiddenGuard achieves 94.7% accuracy with under 50 ms latency, outperforming prior methods while reducing overhead by 67%.
authors: Parupally, Vamshidhar Reddy and Gottam, Monisha
venue: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer and Information Technology (ICCIT)
reason: O trabalho trata diretamente de prompt injection esteganográfico oculto em imagens e propõe detecção e mitigação em tempo real para MLLMs. O resumo apresenta métricas de acurácia, latência e overhead, embora forneça menos detalhes experimentais que outros estudos.

title: Prompt Firewalls for Securing Large Language Model Systems: Threats, Architectures, and Design Trade-offs
abstract: Large Language Models are increasingly deployed as core components of enterprise automation platforms, retrieval-augmented generation systems, and autonomous agentic work-flows. While these systems enable advanced reasoning and decision-making, they also introduce a new attack surface rooted in natural language interaction. Prompt injection and indirect prompt injection attacks exploit the instruction-following behavior of these models, allowing adversaries to manipulate system behavior through untrusted inputs and external context.Prompt Firewalls have emerged as a security mechanism that intercepts and constrain prompt construction before or during model inference. Existing approaches range from lexical filtering and policy enforcement to semantic validation, role-aware parsing, and stateful monitoring across multi-step workflows, each presenting distinct architectural trade-offs.This survey provides a structured and implementation-oriented review of Prompt Firewall research. We examine attack models, design principles, deployment strategies, and enforcement mechanisms, and compare representative approaches to identify strengths, limitations, and open challenges in securing Large Language Model systems.
authors: Hossain, Md. Shojib and Adnan, Md Nasim and Sheikh, Mohammad Nowsin Amin and Rahman, Muhammad Towfiqur
venue: 2026 International Conference on Power, Electronics, Communications, Computing, and Intelligent Infrastructure (PECCII)
reason: O survey é centrado em prompt injection e indirect prompt injection e revisa arquiteturas de prompt firewall, mecanismos de enforcement, modelos de ataque e trade-offs. O contexto inclui RAG, workflows agentivos e entradas externas não confiáveis, com síntese estruturada de abordagens de defesa.

title: External Data Extraction Attacks Against Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
abstract: In recent years, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a key paradigm for enhancing large language models (LLMs). By integrating externally retrieved information, RAG alleviates issues like outdated knowledge and, crucially, insufficient domain expertise. While effective, RAG introduces new risks of external data extraction attacks (EDEAs), where sensitive or copyrighted data in its knowledge base may be extracted verbatim by adversaries. These risks are particularly acute when RAG is used to customize specialized LLM applications with private knowledge bases. Despite initial studies exploring these risks, they often lack a formalized framework, robust attack performance, and comprehensive evaluation, leaving critical questions about real-world EDEA feasibility unanswered. In this paper, we present the first comprehensive study to formalize EDEAs against retrieval-augmented LLMs (RA-LLMs). We first formally define EDEAs and propose a unified framework decomposing their design into three components: extraction instruction, jailbreak operator, and retrieval trigger, under which prior attacks can be considered instances within our framework. Guided by this framework, we develop Secret: a Scalable and EffeCtive exteRnal data Extraction aTtack. Specifically, Secret incorporates (1) an adaptive optimization process using LLMs as optimizers to generate specialized jailbreak prompts for EDEAs, and (2) cluster-focused triggering, an adaptive strategy that alternates between global exploration and local exploitation to efficiently generate effective retrieval triggers. Extensive evaluations across 4 models (including 3 leading commercial LLMs) reveal that Secret significantly outperforms previous attacks, and is highly effective against all 16 tested RAG instances. Notably, Secret successfully extracts 35% of the data from RAG powered by Claude 3.7 Sonnet for the first time, whereas other attacks yield 0% extraction. Secret is also evaluated against potential defenses. Our findings call for urgent attention to this concerning yet largely overlooked emerging threat. Code is available here.
authors: He, Yu and Chen, Yifei and Li, Yiming and Shao, Shuo and Qi, Leyi and Li, Boheng and Tao, Dacheng and Qin, Zhan
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
reason: The central threat is external data extraction from RAG systems rather than prompt injection itself, but the attack framework explicitly incorporates jailbreak operators and optimized jailbreak prompts. It provides a formal attack model, concrete mechanisms, multi-model experiments, defense evaluation, and a highly relevant RAG setting.

title: Graph-Based Prompt Injection Attacks Against Large Language Models
abstract: As Large language models (LLMs) become widely used, injection attacks that induce violent or discriminatory responses from these models are also becoming more frequent. Initially, many attacks used elaborately designed textual prompts, but recently, with the introduction of models that support multi-modality, many attacks using images in addition to textual prompts have been attempted. Injection attacks using only existing text or images are mostly neutralized by latest safe aligned Large language models. In this paper, we present a new method of replacing sensitive words in the prompt with math expressions and performing an injection attack using a graph drawn based on them. By distributing illegal prompts across various input domains, for intrusion attacks against the latest safe aligned LLMs, our proposed approach achieves a very high success rate compared to SOTA existing injection attacks. We hope that the safety of the multimodal LLMs will be further strengthened by understanding the proposed injection attack.
authors: Kwon, Hyeokjin and Kim, Jaebeom and Pak, Wooguil
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
reason: O artigo propõe diretamente um ataque de prompt injection multimodal que substitui termos sensíveis por expressões matemáticas e os distribui em um grafo. O resumo relata alta taxa de sucesso em comparação com ataques SOTA, embora forneça poucos detalhes sobre modelos, métricas e protocolo experimental.

title: Reconstruction-Based Prompt Generation Algorithm for Prompt Injection Attacks
abstract: In order to better bypass the security mechanism of the existing model and verify the vulnerabilities of the model in prompt word injection, we propose a reconstructed prompt generation algorithm (RPGA) to explore the prompt injection attacks of large language models. By combining fictional scenes and template-based, more confusing and diverse prompt words are generated. By dynamically generating prompt words, the invisibility and success rate of attacks are enhanced. Experimental results show that RPGA has a high attack success rate on multiple mainstream large language models, which fully verifies the vulnerability of the current model in prompt word injection attacks. Compared with direct prompt injection and indirect prompt injection, the success rate of reconfiguration prompt injection attack is significantly improved. The result highlights the vulnerability of current large language models in the face of complex prompt word attacks, and provides an important reference for the improvement of subsequent model security mechanisms.
authors: Yu, Zhengyi and Fan, Chunlong
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Neural Networks (AANN)
reason: Prompt injection é o foco central, com um algoritmo de reconstrução para gerar prompts adversariais mais diversos e evasivos. O resumo relata experimentos em múltiplos LLMs e comparação com injeção direta e indireta, embora forneça poucos detalhes sobre modelos e métricas.

title: Automated Framework for Red-Team Prompt Injection Testing of LLMs
abstract: The main aim of this work is to improve Large Language Models (LLMs)security assessment by creating an automated framework for red team prompt injection testing of LLMs. Materials and Methods: The system uses reasoning-based prompt generation together with adaptive feedback to construct its framework. The system compares its performance against baseline random and static attack techniques by testing both methods during 30 prompt iterations. At present, two types of red-teaming models exist which include static models and random models. The automated framework develops better adversarial prompts through model feedback which improves their performance with time. Results: The proposed method reduces the average number of iterations to 15.1, raises the coverage to 74.2%, and raises the attack success rate to 62.3%, which is higher than the rates for static and random attacks, which are 36.8% and 19.4%, respectively. The proposed framework provides an effective LLM security assessment method which outperforms traditional assessment techniques in both speed and accuracy.
authors: K, Manikandan. and S, Bharanidharan. and K, Sudha. and R, Arulalan. and R, Manoja. and M, Chandru.
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Computing, Communication and Green Engineering (CCGE)
reason: Desenvolve um framework automatizado de red teaming especificamente para prompt injection, com geração adaptativa de prompts adversariais. Compara abordagens estática e aleatória e reporta cobertura, ASR e número de iterações.

title: JailSmash: Lightweight Jailbreaking of LLM Applications on Android Smartphones
abstract: The rapid growth of LLM APPs brings potential security risks, particularly jailbreaking attacks. These attacks involve bypassing LLM security mechanisms through carefully designed prompts to generate harmful or unethical content, posing threats to both individuals and organizations. We developed a lightweight jailbreak tool called JailSmash, which leverages jailbreak templates based on in-context learning (ICL) and strategies to guide third-party large language models in automatically generating jailbreak test sets. This tool also enables automated interaction and evaluation of jailbreak results with LLM apps on Android smartphones. Furthermore, we used JailSmash to conduct jailbreak security assessments on 30 mainstream LLM apps, thereby validating the effectiveness of the tool.
authors: Tian, Chen and Yuan, Qi and Liu, Xiaoli and Yan, Ying
venue: 2025 IEEE 7th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
reason: O artigo apresenta uma ferramenta para geração automatizada de conjuntos de jailbreak e avaliação automática de aplicações LLM em Android. A aplicação da ferramenta a 30 apps fornece evidência empírica relevante para red teaming e avaliação de ataques.

title: SecureRag: Preventing Sensitive Information Leakage In Rag Pipelines
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation is most commonly used to combine large language models with an external knowledge base in an attempt to ground them. This significantly improves the performance in terms of factual information, but sometimes these pipelines can also expose sensitive information if not handled properly. In this work, SecureRag a framework is presented which is designed to reduce the leakage of sensitive information in these systems. Synthetic datasets were created for six domains including legal, financial, healthcare, government, and e-commerce using Python Faker Library. To implement the SecureRag system, filtering layers were implemented that redacts confidential content before it reaches the large language model. The implementation began with regular expression based filters which were later enhanced with Microsoft Presidio based filters. The implementation was evaluated with multiple tests and large language models including MiniLm, Gemini Flash 2.5, BERT-QA. The RAG system was tested against various scenarios of adversarial attacks such as prompt injections, Base64-encoded data, and needle-in-the-haystack challenges. The results show that SecureRag can effectively prevent sensitive information leakage in RAG pipelines while keeping the retrieval performance intact, this offers a safer approach for RAG pipelines.
authors: Mishra, Nidhi and Rai, Kanchan and Sharma, Dhruv
venue: 2025 Second International Conference on Pioneering Developments in Computer Science & Digital Technologies (IC2SDT)
reason: The work proposes and evaluates a RAG defense framework against sensitive-data leakage, explicitly testing prompt injections alongside other adversarial scenarios. Its RAG setting, filtering defenses, synthetic datasets, multiple models, and attack tests make it highly relevant.

title: Partial-Reps: Defending Large Language Models against Jailbreaks via Partial Repetition
abstract: Jailbreaks in Large Language Models (LLMs) compromise their security and force them to generate malicious content. State-of-the-Art (SOTA) solutions either query the same model multiple times to use the model itself as a jailbreak detector, or use a separate classifier trained to detect malicious outputs. Training a separate classifier is inefficient when defending against jailbreaks on which the model hasn't been trained, whereas the self-querying solution has the issue that querying the same model multiple times incurs overhead in time and computational power. Addressing the issue of self-querying, we propose a novel approach that attempts to achieve better accuracy and reduce computational complexity by leveraging tokenization. We experiment with the approach on eight benchmark datasets and three benchmark LLMs. We observe that our approach preserves the accuracy while significantly reducing the computational complexity.
authors: Gujjari, Neha and Williams, Dhruva Menon and Ravi, Nagarathna and Nallana, Mithun Babu and Hasan Ansari, Md Talib
venue: 2025 Second International Conference on Pioneering Developments in Computer Science & Digital Technologies (IC2SDT)
reason: The paper directly proposes a jailbreak defense intended to reduce the cost of self-querying detection. It is evaluated on eight benchmark datasets and three LLMs, providing direct empirical evidence on defense effectiveness and efficiency.

title: Prompt Injection Detection via Key Feature Integration in Large Language Models
abstract: This study proposes Total-Layer Detection (TLD), a novel framework that integrally utilizes all layers of a Large Language Model to detect prompt injection attacks effectively. To address the computational inefficiency arising from high-dimensional data, we selectively utilized only the core features decisive for attack identification. Experiments demonstrated that TLD achieves higher accuracy and superior efficiency compared to single-layer approaches by efficiently reducing the feature dimensionality from the concatenated total-layer vector while enhancing detection precision.
authors: Won, Seyeon and Pak, Wooguil
venue: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Information and Communication (ICAIIC)
reason: Propõe um framework específico para detecção de prompt injection utilizando características selecionadas de todas as camadas do LLM. Experimentos reportam ganhos de precisão e eficiência frente a abordagens de camada única.

title: Enhancing Jailbreak Defense with Diverse Perturbation Combinations
abstract: While aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences can prevent undesired outputs, recent research indicates that jailbreak prompts can easily bypass such safeguards, resulting in the generation of prohibited content. In response, perturbation strategies are explored to damage attacks. However, some methods entail iterative checks of prompt subsequences, introducing uncontrollable complexity. Moreover, certain defenses relying on random perturbation are inadequate in disrupting malicious requests, leading to the defense being bypassed. Others depending on a single type of perturbation may incorrectly respond to benign requests while countering attacks. To address these issues, we propose a simple but effective defense strategy called Diverse Perturbation Combinations (DPC). It refines existing perturbations and achieves enough interference on attacks through targeted perturbation, enabling defense against multiple jailbreak attacks. Moreover, by strategically combining different operations, DPC ensures stable detection of benign or harmful requests. We conduct exhaustive theoretical analysis, providing effectiveness guarantees for the defense. Experimental validation on datasets featuring diverse jailbreak prompts across multiple closed-source and open-source LLMs further confirms the empirical effectiveness of our approach.
authors: Wu, Tingting and Gao, Qi and Yu, Zhiwen
venue: 2026 13th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
reason: Propõe uma defesa específica contra jailbreak baseada em combinações de perturbações e a valida em múltiplos datasets e LLMs. O foco é diretamente alinhado à mitigação de ataques, com evidência teórica e experimental.

title: EVA: Editing for Versatile Alignment Against Jailbreaks
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities but remain vulnerable to jailbreaking attacks, where adversaries exploit textual or visual triggers to bypass safety guardrails. Recent defenses typically rely on safety fine-tuning or external filters to reduce the model’s likelihood of producing harmful content. While effective to some extent, these methods often incur significant computational overheads and suffer from the safety utility trade-off, degrading the model’s performance on benign tasks. To address these challenges, we propose EVA (Editing for Versatile Alignment against Jailbreaks), a novel framework that pioneers the application of direct model editing for safety alignment. EVA reframes safety alignment as a precise knowledge correction task. Instead of retraining massive parameters, EVA identifies and surgically edits specific neurons responsible for the model’s susceptibility to harmful instructions, while leaving the vast majority of the model unchanged. By localizing the updates, EVA effectively neutralizes harmful behaviors without compromising the model’s general reasoning capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EVA outperforms baselines in mitigating jailbreaks across both LLMs and VLMs, offering a precise and efficient solution for post-deployment safety alignment.
authors: Wang, Yi and Qiu, Hongye and Xu, Yue and Yang, Sibei and Qin, Zhan and Huang, Minlie and Wang, Wenjie
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
reason: Jailbreak é o fenômeno central e a contribuição principal é uma defesa por edição direta de neurônios associados à suscetibilidade a instruções nocivas. O resumo relata experimentos extensos em LLMs e VLMs contra baselines, com preservação de utilidade.

title: Optimizing Transformer Models for Prompt Jailbreak Attack Detection in AI Assistant Systems
abstract: Integrating AI-powered assistants in different areas has changed how people retrieve information. Users can now get quick responses, use the service whenever needed, and handle inquiries well. However, relying on these systems has increasingly raised worries about their safety and reliability, especially when facing threats like prompt injection or jailbreak attacks. These attacks take advantage of the weaknesses of large language models (LLMs) by changing input prompts to create harmful, biased, or misleading results. This paper examines prompt jailbreak attacks in ChatGPT-based assistant chatbots, especially in education. It examines the weaknesses in these systems and suggests ways to detect these attacks by fine-tuning various Transformer models. The research also includes adding prompt jailbreak attack detection in a virtual assistant application for university use. This aims to ensure teachers and students can interact safely and rely on the system. Through rigorous experimentation and evaluation, we demonstrate the practicality and effectiveness of our detection methods, providing reassurance and confidence in the face of AI security challenges. Our studies emphasize the need for robust AI chatbots and offer practical solutions to preserve the integrity of AI-driven tools.
authors: Tien, Le Anh and Van Huong, Pham
venue: 2024 1st International Conference On Cryptography And Information Security (VCRIS)
reason: O foco é detectar prompt injection e jailbreak em assistentes baseados em ChatGPT por meio de fine-tuning de diferentes modelos Transformer. O trabalho inclui implementação em um assistente universitário e experimentação para avaliar a eficácia dos detectores.

title: Comparative Analysis of Jailbreaking Techniques for Large Language Models: A Systematic Evaluation Framework
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit varying degrees of vulnerability to adversarial attacks that bypass their safety mechanisms. This paper presents a systematic evaluation framework for analyzing different jailbreaking methodologies across multiple model architectures. We introduce a comprehensive framework for quantifying the effectiveness of the jailbreaking technique in 13 distinct categories of harmful content. Our framework enables reproducible comparisons between different attack vectors and provides insight into scale-dependent vulnerability patterns. The evaluations performed on the framework shows how model architecture and parameter count influence resistance to different attack types, revealing important relationships between model capabilities and security vulnerabilities.
authors: Pablo VellosilloAna Garcia-FornesJose SuchElena del Val
venue: Computational Intelligence in Security for Information Systems
reason: Apresenta um framework sistemático para comparar técnicas de jailbreak entre arquiteturas e categorias de conteúdo nocivo. O foco em comparação reproduzível de vetores de ataque e padrões de vulnerabilidade é diretamente útil para caracterizar ataques e protocolos de avaliação.

title: Detection Method for Prompt Injection by Integrating Pre-trained Model and Heuristic Feature Engineering
abstract: To address prompt injection threats in LLMs, we propose DMPI-PMHFE, a dual-channel feature fusion framework that integrates DeBERTa with heuristic feature engineering. The framework transforms input text into semantic vectors while extracting explicit structural features through attack-pattern-based heuristic rules. Features from both channels are fused via fully connected networks for final classification. This approach mitigates limitations of single-channel feature extraction. Experimental results demonstrate that DMPI-PMHFE outperforms existing methods in accuracy, recall, and F1-score across diverse benchmark datasets. When deployed on mainstream LLMs (GLM-4, LLaMA 3, Qwen 2.5, and GPT-4o), it significantly reduces attack success rates.

title: Secure Guard: A Semantic-Based Jailbreak Prompt Detection Framework for Protecting Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have made significant progress in the field of natural language processing. Through training, they can understand natural language texts and demonstrate impressive abilities in language processing and generation. However, due to the presence of “competing objectives” and “mismatched generalization” in LLMs, they are susceptible to jailbreak attacks. This type of attack can bypass the safety alignment mechanism of the model, causing LLMs to generate inappropriate or harmful content. To address this issue, this paper proposes a semantic-based jailbreak attack detection method. We have designed a hybrid neural network architecture called Secure Guard to improve the detection effectiveness and accuracy of jailbreak attacks. Compared with existing defense methods, this model identifies harmful content by analyzing input semantic information, solving the low coverage and false alarm problems associated with jailbreak attacks. Experimental results have shown that Secure Guard achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple test sets.
authors: Sixin FangKe ChengJixin ZhangZheng QinMingwu Zhang
venue: Information and Communications Security

title: JADE: Jailbreak-Aware Dynamic Defense Enhancer for LLMs Via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Adversarial attacks pose significant threats to Large Language Models (LLMs), enabling malicious actors to generate harmful content through carefully crafted prompts. To address this challenge, we propose JADE: Jailbreak-Aware Dynamic Defense Enhancer, a novel reinforcement learning framework that dynamically enhances LLM robustness against jailbreak attacks. JADE employs a three-model architecture—Jailbreak Prompt Optimizer, Target Model, and Safety Evaluator—that engage in closed-loop adversarial training using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). The framework enables continuous co-evolution of attack and defense strategies through iterative policy updates. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate JADE's superior performance, significantly reducing attack success rates while maintaining model utility compared to state-of-the-art defense methods.

O resumo informa experimentos em múltiplos benchmarks e redução de ASR preservando utilidade, embora não detalhe valores quantitativos.

title: To Protect the LLM Agent Against the Prompt Injection Attack with Polymorphic Prompt
abstract: LLM agents are widely used as agents for customer support, content generation, and code assistance. However, they are vulnerable to prompt injection attacks, where adversarial inputs manipulate the model’s behavior. Traditional defenses like input sanitization, guard models, and guardrails are either cumbersome or ineffective. In this paper, we propose a novel, lightweight defense mechanism called Polymorphic Prompt Assembling (PPA), which protects against prompt injection with near-zero overhead. The approach is based on the insight that prompt injection requires guessing and breaking the structure of the system prompt. By dynamically varying the structure of system prompts, PPA prevents attackers from predicting the prompt structure, thereby enhancing security without compromising performance. We conducted experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of PPA against existing attacks and compared it with other defense methods.

title: Secure MCP-Based Tool-Augmented RAG for Industrial IoT Diagnostics Under Indirect Prompt Injection, Retrieval Poisoning, and Modality Outages
abstract: Industrial IoT diagnostics require integrating diverse evidence streams, such as telemetry, event logs, configuration snapshots, and operational knowledge bases, while adhering to safety and security requirements. Tool-augmented retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) facilitates this integration by merging retrieval processes with the regulated use of tools. In Operational Technology (OT) settings, two primary risks associated with deployment are: (i) indirect prompt injection through retrieved materials or tool outputs, which can disrupt the model context and result in behavior that contradicts established policies; and (ii) limited visibility caused by tool failures, gaps in telemetry, and delayed logging, which diminishes evidential support and raises the chances of producing unsubstantiated outputs. This paper examines a protocol-aligned architecture that integrates MCP-exposed tools within a defense-in-depth RAG pipeline. The approach employs hybrid retrieval and reranking, instruction-aware content filtering, typed least-privilege tool mediation with audit logging, evidence-bound generation with citation enforcement, and outage-aware abstention policies. An OT-oriented stress-test suite is defined based on prior RAG security evaluations, and utility, security, and degradation metrics are reported using a proprietary multi-site IIoT dataset. The findings indicate the importance of treating retrieval and tool interfaces as distinct security boundaries in industrial diagnostic assistants.
authors: Ersoy, Pınar and Erşahin, Mustafa

title: Efficient Prompt Security Detection for LLM Service Deployment in Edge-Cloud Networks
abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved revolutionary advancements in natural language processing, their inherent vulnerability to prompt injection attacks has raised significant security concerns. Existing security detection approaches for LLM deployment often fail to fully leverage edge-cloud collaboration and largely overlook the issue of user heterogeneity, resulting in reduced detection efficiency and security risks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Belief-updating and User-aware Security (BUUAS) framework for LLM service deployment in edge–cloud networks. BUUAS integrates a Bayesian-inspired belief update method with a belief-weighted contextual multi-armed bandit (BWCB) mechanism to achieve dynamic and user-aware scheduling of security detection tasks. This design enables the system to prioritize high-risk requests while improving overall task allocation and execution efficiency. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that BUUAS outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of detection accuracy, network throughput, and resource efficiency in dynamic network conditions characterized by fluctuating user loads and varying malicious user ratios.
authors: Chen, Wenjing and Cui, Jie and Huang, Wenjie and Zhang, Jing and Wei, Lu and Min, Geyong

title: Evolving Security in LLMs: A Study of Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly popular, powering a wide range of applications. Their widespread use has sparked concerns, especially through jailbreak attacks that bypass safety measures to produce harmful content. In this paper, we present a comprehensive security analysis of large language models (LLMs), addressing critical research questions on the evolution and determinants of model safety. Specifically, we begin by identifying the most effective techniques for detecting jailbreak attacks. Next, we investigate whether newer versions of LLMs offer improved security compared to their predecessors. We also assess the impact of model size on overall security and explore the potential benefits of integrating multiple defense strategies to enhance the security. Our study evaluates both open-source (e.g., LLaMA and Mistral) and closedsource models (e.g., GPT-4) by employing four state-of-the-art attack techniques and assessing the efficacy of three new defensive approaches. Our code and dataset can be found at [1].
